deep.reconstruction:
This is not a mathematical derivation. It is a calendrical table headed 'Geburtsjahre Göttingischer Professoren' (birth years of Göttingen professors), with Euler, Lagrange and Newton added as comparisons. The columns are, row by row:
(i) name;
(ii) birth year, where a blank means the same year as the row above;
(iii) birth month and day;
(iv) a two-digit number. This is the age at which the man took up his Göttingen post. Examples: Gauss 1777+30=1807, Harding 1765+40=1805, Blumenbach 1752+24=1776, Thibaut 1775+27=1802, Stromeyer 1776+29=1805, the elder Eichhorn 1752+36=1788, the jurist Eichhorn 1781+36=1817.
(v) '†' followed by the date of death;
(vi) a five-digit number, which is the exact length of life in days, N = date(death) − date(birth).
The vertical bracket on the right marks the deceased entries. The facing page repeats the day counts in its margin. The entries were clearly added over many years, since Mitscherlich's death on 6 Jan 1854 is entered.

Method (my reconstruction):
N = 365·(full years) + (number of 29 Februaries passed) + (days in the remaining fraction of a year).
Gregorian rules are used, so 1800 is not a leap year.
- Worked example, Euler (Gregorian dates): 1707-04-15 to 1783-04-15 is 76·365 + 19 = 27759. April 15 to Sept 18 adds 156. Total 27915, as written.
- Lagrange: 1736-01-25 to 1813-04-10 = 28199, as written.
- Newton: no dates are written; only 30766 appears. Newton's Old-Style dates are 25 Dec 1642 to 20 Mar 1726/7, with the Julian leap year 1700 counted. Equivalently, the New-Style dates 4 Jan 1643 to 31 Mar 1727. Either way the count is 30766, as written.

I recomputed every row. Correct as written: Stromeier (death Jun 27 confirmed by the count), Reuss, Mayer, Blumenbach, Eichhorn, Tychsen, Mitscherlich, Pott, Heeren, Stäudlin, Schulze, Benecke, Hugo, Schrader, Hempel, Harding, 'Artaud', Bunsen, Himly, Thibaut, Langenbeck (with Dec 8), Euler, Lagrange, Newton.

Rows where the birth date is missing, inverted from the count:
- Böhmer: implies born 29 Oct 1753.
- Meister: implies born 28 Oct 1755.

Rows that are inconsistent with the dates written on the page are listed under errors.

The page is a record of personal and academic chronology. It shows Gauss's well-known fondness for counting days lived. It contains no mathematics beyond exact calendar arithmetic.
errors: Planck (b. 1751, no day given; G. J. Planck was born 15 Nov 1751) to † 31 Aug 1833 is 29874 days. Gauss's 29982 corresponds to a birth date of 30 Jul 1751, which is the same month and day as Reuss in the row above. This looks like a mistaken ditto, a 108-day error.
Bouterwek: 15 Apr 1766 to 9 Aug 1828 is 22761 days. The written 22517 corresponds to a birth date of 15 Dec 1766, a discrepancy of 244 days.

Sartorius: with the dittoed year 1766, 25 Aug 1766 to 24 Aug 1828 is 22644 days, not 22629 (off by 15). The true birth year is 1765, which would give 23009. The written 22629 fits 25 Aug 1766 to 9 Aug 1828, apparently taking Bouterwek's death day.
Bauer: 16 Aug 1772 to 1 Jun 1843 is 25855 days; the page has 25853 (off by 2).
Stromeyer: 2 Aug 1776 to 18 Aug 1835 is 21564 days; the page reads 21584 (off by 20). This may be a 6/8 reading ambiguity rather than Gauss's slip.
Tychsen's death is usually given as 23 Oct 1834; Gauss has 24 Oct, and his count is consistent with the 24th.
Langenbeck's birth is usually given as 5 Dec 1776; Gauss uses Dec 8 (overwritten on the page), and his count is consistent with Dec 8.
Sartorius' birth year is 1765, but the blank year column implies 1766.

results.what: Exact life spans in days computed from birth and death dates, including a Julian (Old Style) span for Newton
results.usually_credited_to: Standard calendrical arithmetic (Scaliger's Julian period, 1583; routine practice in astronomy)

results.what: Table of birth dates, ages at appointment and death dates of Göttingen professors

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely calendrical bookkeeping. Gauss's habit of counting days lived (his own and others') is well documented. The page is of minor biographical interest only, for instance for the few slipped counts.

checkable.asserts: Newton (O.S. 25 Dec 1642 to 20 Mar 1726/7) lived 30766 days
Stromeier's count implies death on June 27, 1830
Planck's count corresponds to a birth date of 30 Jul 1751
Correct Planck count with true birthday 15 Nov 1751
Bouterwek: correct value differs from written 22517
Bouterwek: written value corresponds to a birth date of 15 Dec 1766

transcription_corrections: Stromeier's death date is Jun 27, 1830; the reading '27' is confirmed by the day count 29242.
Mitscherlich's total 34075 is confirmed; the '[?]' can be removed.
In the Hempel row, the death year is overwritten to 1834, which agrees with 24315.
Langenbeck's birth day is 'Dec 8', overwritten; it agrees with 27074.
The Newton line carries only the total 30766, written below Lagrange's 28199; no dates are given.
'Artaud' is an uncertain reading of the name; his dates (4 Jun 1769 to 20 Apr 1837) agree with 24791.
The row order on the page has 'Sartorius' squeezed above an overwritten 'Schrader 1767 Jan 1 35 † Oct. 22. 1836 25496'.
